bullets.text: The governing-law heading now includes a class action waiver, and a new paragraph requires each party to bring claims only in an individual capacity. Neither party may participate as a plaintiff, claimant, or class member in a class, collective, consolidated, private attorney general, or representative proceeding in court or arbitration, though either may still join a class-wide, collective, or representative settlement. New York courts' exclusive jurisdiction is also extended to disputes about whether the Arbitration Agreement applies and can be enforced.

bullets.text: Mandatory individual arbitration now covers claims that arose before this Arbitration Agreement or any prior one, replacing language limited to claims arising during or after termination. Courts, not the arbitrator, also have exclusive authority over which version of the Arbitration Agreement applies.

the substantive and procedural provisions of the Federal Arbitration Act (and not state arbitration law) apply

bullets.text: The arbitration clause now says the Federal Arbitration Act's substantive and procedural provisions, and not state arbitration law, govern interpretation and enforcement. An arbitration demand must also disclose any person or entity funding the case or holding a financial interest in it.

The arbitrator may make rulings and resolve any disagreements as to the payment and reimbursement of fees or expenses at any time during the proceeding and upon request from either party made within fourteen (14) days of the arbitrator's ruling on the merits.

bullets.text: An arbitrator's ruling in one user's case is now expressly not binding and has no preclusive effect in proceedings involving different users. The Terms also remove the arbitrator's stated authority to resolve fee and expense reimbursement disputes within 14 days after a merits ruling.
